layout_note: MIXED-SCRIPT single-column epistle page (1582 Rheims NT): Colossians 3:18-25 body (top) with a full-width ANNOTATIONS block for CHAP. III below it, then CHAP. IIII heading + italic Argument + woodcut historiated drop-cap 'Y' opening Colossians 4:1-5. Left margin carries roman-italic scripture cross-references (braced to verse groups); right margin carries small-face topical notes. The page's single piece of GREEK type is the word in the Col 3:24 right-margin 'Retribution' note (read as ἀπόδοσις; see uncertain[] re ἀνταπόδοσις). THREE glyph regimes: roman BODY uses a real single-sort 'w' (rendered w/W per the NT-1582 resolution); the ITALIC argument is borderline (rendered vv from the visible strokes, flagged); the SMALL apparatus face (ANNOTATIONS + all margin notes) sets genuine 'vv' (revvard, vvorkes, vvhich, vvorſhipping, nevv, vve) — rendered vv. The italic annotation quotations 'Couetouſnes is idolatrie' etc. are English translations in italic ROMAN, not Greek script. Inter-word spacing (incl. French spacing before high punctuation, and tight commas like 'huſbands,as') is transcribed best-effort/approximate. Digitization artefacts excluded.

apparatus.subtitle: CHAP. III.
apparatus.note: centered two-line display header opening the chapter-III annotation block.

apparatus.lemma: Auarice, vvhich is the ſeruice of idols.
apparatus.text: Here is a maruelous impudent and foliſh corruption in the vulgar Engliſh Bible printed the yere 1577 and (as it ſeemeth) moſt authoriſed. Vvhere for their errour againſt the Images of Chriſt and his Saincts, and to make image and idol,al one: the tranſlator, for that vvhich the Apoſtle ſaith in Greeke, Couetouſnes is idolatrie, maketh him to ſay in Engliſh, Couetouſnes is vvorſhipping of images : as alſo Eph. 5, ✱ he tranſlateth thus, The couetous perſon is a vvorſhipper of images : for that vvhich the Apoſtle ſaith, The couetous man is an idolater, meaning ſpiritual idolatrie, becauſe he maketh money his God. In vvhich ſenſe to call this ſpiritual idolatrie,vvorſhipping of images, is to ridiculous, and muſt needes procede of blinde hereſie.
italic_spans: Auarice, vvhich is the ſeruice of idols
The couetous perſon is a vvorſhipper of images
The couetous man is an idolater
apparatus.note: The 'in Greeke' quotations are English renderings set in ITALIC ROMAN, not Greek type. Number printed reads as '9' but the lemma (Auarice=service of idols) is unambiguously Col 3:5 — anchored 3:5; see uncertain[]. '✱' after 'Eph. 5,' is a small printer's reference mark of uncertain exact glyph (see uncertain[]).

apparatus.text: By this and the vvhole diſcourſe of this chapter conteining an exhortation to good life, and to put on the habite of the nevv man vvith al vertues : vve may ſee, our iuſtice in Chriſt to be a very qualitie and forme inherent in our ſoul,adorning the ſame, and not an imputation onely of Chriſtes righteouſnes, or a hiding onely of our ſinnes and vvickednes,vvhich the Heretikes falſely affirme to remaine in vs after baptiſme and alvvaies during life. See S. Auguſtine de pec. mer. & remiſ. li. 2. c. 7. & cont. Iulian. li. 6. c. 7.
italic_spans: de pec. mer. & remiſ. li. 2. c. 7. & cont. Iulian. li. 6. c. 7.
apparatus.note: Anchored to the old-man/new-man passage (Col 3:9-10); the lemma 'Doing on the nevv' concerns 'putting on the new man' (v10). Augustine citation set italic.

apparatus.text: He exhorteth to inſtance in praier, 5 and to vviſedom in behauiour. 7 He ſendeth Tychicus. 10 He doeth commendations, 15 and inioyneth to be done.

greek.letters: ἀ(alpha+smooth-breathing) π ό(omicron+acute) δ ο σ(lunate) ι ς(final-sigma)
greek.gloss_printed_en: which ſignifieth rendering one for another
greek.note: THE page's sole Greek-type word. Read as ἀπόδοσις: a single alpha (with smooth breathing) then a heavily over-inked π whose right side merges into ό, then δοσις. Critically only ONE alpha is present and ό follows the π directly, so there is no room for a 'ντ' cluster — hence ἀπόδοσις, not ἀνταπόδοσις. See uncertain[] for the ἀνταπόδοσις question (the verse's actual Greek, and the exact sense of the gloss 'rendering one for another').

uncertain.note: PRIMARY GREEK UNCERTAINTY. Transcribed diplomatically as ἀπόδοσις (α + over-inked π + ό + δ ο σ ι ς). The verse's actual Greek is ἀνταπόδοσιν/ἀνταπόδοσις (Col 3:24, 'the retribution of the inheritance'), and the printed gloss 'rendering one for another' matches the reciprocal sense of ἀντ-απόδοσις precisely. HOWEVER the glyphs show only one alpha with ό immediately after the (single, heavily inked) π, leaving no 'ντ' cluster visible — so the printed form reads ἀπόδοσις (possibly a compositor's omission of the ἀντ- prefix, or the annotator citing the simplex). If a human reviewer can confirm hidden strokes in the over-inked π-blob, the intended word is ἀνταπόδοσις. Breathing/accent read as smooth-breathing on α and acute on ό.

The italic old-style figure before 'Auarice, which is the ſeruice of idols' reads as '9' at scan resolution, but that lemma is unambiguously Col 3:5 (the only avarice/idols verse in Colossians). Anchored to 3:5 on lemma-text evidence; printed digit may be a mis-set '9' for '5', or an old-style italic '5' misread as '9'. Reviewer should verify the digit.

Rendered 'vviſedom' (vv) from the two visibly separate strokes, but the NT-1582 italic argument face was resolved as a REAL cursive 'w' on the 2John GT (same edition). Borderline w/vv — flag for the corrector. Only w-instance in the argument.

Rendered with 'W' per the NT-1582 resolution that the roman body owns a real single-sort 'w' (task note + 2John GT). On the page these sentence-initial caps are set in the vv-style W sort (appear as 'Vv'); rendered W, not VV (VV is reserved for display titling caps, of which there are none on this page).

A small printer's reference mark/floret of uncertain exact glyph sits between 'Eph. 5,' and 'he tranſlateth thus'; represented as ✱. Possibly points to Eph 5:5 (the covetous-idolater verse) rather than being a numeral. Reviewer to confirm.

uncertain.location: body + margin notes: three-dot reference mark
uncertain.note: The reference mark linking the Col 3:24 gloss (body '∵ retri-') to its 'Retribution' note, and the Col 4:3 body ('∵ for vs alſo') to its 'S.Paul' note, is a three-dot cluster; exact orientation (∴ vs ∵) is not resolvable at this resolution — rendered ∵ uniformly.
'opē' = 'open' (o+p+macron/tilde vowel nasal abbreviation, ē→en). Preserved as printed.

Spacing is transcribed best-effort. This edition mixes tight commas with no following space ('huſbands,as', 'Fathers,prouoke', 'fleſh,not', 'doe,worke', 'inheritance.Serue', 'alſo,that') and French spacing before high punctuation (' :'). Not every space was individually zoom-verified; an aligner/reviewer should refine.

long-ſ transcribed glyph-by-glyph, not by position. 'ſhal' (3:24, 3:25) read with long-ſ; ſubiect/huſbands/fleſh/ſimplicitie/ſeruants/ſeruing/ſhal/iuſt/manifeſt etc. per visible glyph. Not exhaustively re-zoomed at every s — reviewer should spot-check.

method: visual-multimodal read of the S8 hires jp2 raster (5910x8686) with ~30 targeted PIL crops upscaled 1.6-7x plus contrast/threshold enhancement of the Greek word and the two annotation lemma-figures; DR/Vulgate content used only to confirm verse span and the Greek verse-word, never as a spelling oracle. Greek word resolved by glyph-count + threshold analysis of the over-inked π.
confidence: HIGH on the scripture body wording, verse structure, marks, cross-references, and annotation text. MEDIUM-HIGH on the Greek word being ἀπόδοσις as printed (HIGH that it is not ἀνταπόδοσις by glyph count, but flagged because the verse-word and gloss point to ἀνταπόδοσις). MEDIUM on: the two annotation lemma-figures (italic 5/9 ambiguity), the argument w/vv call, the '✱' Eph.5 mark, and exact French spacing. Body w/W follows the authoritative NT-1582 real-w resolution rather than a per-instance call.
